newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market debt focus fixed on Brazil-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt focus fixed on Brazil-dealers.

text.p: The focus of the Brady market continued on Brazil, with technical trade amid swapping of Brazilian assets by Asian accounts, dealers said on Thursday.
"Trade is still very much on Brazil -- selling pars and buying C's and 27's (the the new global)," a dealer said. "There is a lot of technical trade -- swapping one asset for another," he added.
Brazil DISC Z were bid at 83.625 at 1200 GMT, up 0.375 point. Brazil "C" were bid at 79.625, up 0.125 point and Brazil PAR were bid at 66.625, up 0.25 point.
Brazil's $3.0 billion 30-year global bond was the best bid at present, dealers said.
It was launched to yield 395 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and was last trading at 370 b.p. over, 25 b.p tighter.
"It is by far the most liquid and largest of all emerging market globals," a dealer said. "We see buyers at 375 b.p. over and sellers at 365 b.p."
There is speculation Argentina, Peru and Venezuela will follow suit with similar Brady buy-back deals, using Mexico and Brazil as a benchmark, dealers said.
"It would make sense for them to do it," a dealer said.

Brazil was also boosted by news of the re-election amendment, analysts said. Brazil's Senate gave its second and final approval to a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election next year.
Venezuela was well bid amid speculation the money raised from auctioning of oil licenses might be used to buy Brady debt back. Venezuela netted $1.5 billion on 12 oil contracts.

News that the cabinet has approved the budget for 1998 was also positive. Venezuela's cabinet of ministers approved Wednesday an 11.2 trillion bolivar ($23.3 billion) budget proposal for 1998, up from 10.2 trillion bolivars in 1997.
There was also talk of Venezuela's upcoming Eurobond. Venezuela plans to set $315 million 10-year Eurobond via ING Barings.
Venez PARS were bid at 76.750, up +0.250
point. Venez DCBS were bid at 91.750, up 0.375 point. Venez FLIRBS were bid at 91.125 and Venez DISC were bid at 86.500.

Dealers said there was not much going on in Eastern Europe. They said there was some profit-taking on dollar Vnesh bonds after recent gains on reports from the "local press" saying it was optimistic on the timing of Russian loan restructuring.
In addition Deutsche Bank said Wednesday the documentation for the restructuring had been finalized and would be sent to the Russian government for its formal approval.
Russian VN US$ were bid at 88.375. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
